newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Sharon met PLO's Abu Mazen on peace.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Sharon met PLO's Abu Mazen on peace.

text.p: Hardline Israeli cabinet minister Ariel Sharon met a top PLO official this month for talks on advancing the peace process, Israeli and Palestinian officials said on Friday.

Sharon, tipped to become finance minister in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet, has been one of the government's fiercest opponents of peace deals with the PLO, branding Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat a "terrorist".

"They both said the talks were conducted in a positive atmosphere. They talked for about two-and-a-half hours on ways to advance the peace process," said Israeli-Arab legislator Abdulwahab Darawshe, who initiated the meeting between Sharon and Mahmoud Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen.
He said the two men met at Sharon's home in southern Israel. PLO officials confirmed the meeting took place.

Abbas, an architect of the landmark 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal, resigned last March as head of the Palestinian negotiating team over Israel's decision to withdraw troops from only small parts of the West Bank, contrary to the PLO's expectations.
That decision coupled with Israel's subsequent groundbreadking of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem plunged peacemaking with the PLO into crisis.
Sharon, a backer of Jewish settlement expansion in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, has demanded a seat on Netanyahu's three-member "kitchen cabinet" which directs Israeli peace moves.
Political analysts have said Foreign Minister David Levy and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai oppose giving the hawkish ex-general a place in the inner team.
